newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to meet EMU deficit criteria in 97 - Waigel.
newsitem.headline: Germany to meet EMU deficit criteria in 97 - Waigel.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Wednesday that combined federal, state and municipal budget deficits in 1997 would be lower than the ceiling set in the Maastricht Treaty on European economic and monetary union.

Waigel told reporters after a meeting with of the government's financial planning council that the states and local authorities were committed to bringing budget deficits next year within the government target of 2.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
The Maastricht Treaty requires members of monetary union to restrict budget deficits to three percent and total public sector debt to 60 percent of GDP.
Waigel said that the great majority of federal states and municipal governments were in step with the federal government budget consolidation programme.

As a result, finance ministry data forecast a 1997 public sector deficit of 99.5 billion marks -- the federal budget deficit would be 53.3 billion marks and the 24.5 billion marks for the states. The remainder is accounted for by local authorities and special budgets.
